texts.preamble: Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.7171/2023 Kabc0B0169562023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21)
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 06.10.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 06.10.2023 at about 09.20 p.m., the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-U-9805 along with pillion rider slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing om moving vehicles and by wearing head guard on Mahadevapura Service Road, at that time one Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-6903 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came to main road at a high speed and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035 and the said Scooter came and dashed against petitioner's motorcycle. Due to forced impact, petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and petitioner sustained grevious injuries and pillion rider sustained simple injuries. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and conveyance charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 44 years, the petitioner was working as delivery boy and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their counsels and filed written statements separately. The respondent No.1 in his written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154932424/ 2 submitted that, the petitioner only riding his vehicles recklessly but also talking to his friend who was also riding scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035. At that point of time the scooter rider bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035 stated supra has suddenly came to the middle of the road without observing the vehicle coming from opposite side i.e., swift car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-6903 belong to this respondent and driven by its driver. Though the driver of the car tried to avoid hitting the scooter by applying the brake, he could not suddenly control the vehicle and hit the scooter. The said scooter in turn hit the motorcycle of the petitioner and due to the said impact both rider and the pillion fell down. Hence, the said accident has occurred due to the reckless and careless driving of both scooter and motorcycle rider. The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending car and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent submitted that, the petitioner/rider of the Hero Passion motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-U-9805 was riding the same without having valid driving license and insurance in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and has not exercised proper care and caution and himself fallen on road and sustained injuries and he has suffered self negligence of self-accident. Further, this respondent submitted that, this petition is bad for mis-joinder of necessary parties. Further, this respondent submitted that, the facts have been twisted and given wrong description and a false charge-sheet has been made against the alleged driver of the alleged Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-6903. Further, the alleged car is commercial vehicle and it was plying without valid permit as on the date of accident. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 170, 134(c), 158(6) of M. V. Act. Further both the respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. On the other hand, GPA Holder of respondent No.1 is examined as RW.1 and got marked a document at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
texts.arguments: 17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 08 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.1,60,000/-. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,60,000/- towards medical expenses. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was delivery boy and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2023. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision. The petitioner to prove her disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total physical disability of 36.16% and that of whole body disability at 18.08%. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
